title: Stochastic Domination of Gaussian Maxima by the Regular Simplex
summary: Let $n\ge2$, and let $X=(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$ be a centered Gaussian vector with $\mathrm{Var}(X_i)=1$ for every $i$. Let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_n$ be independent standard Gaussians, and put $\overline{Z}=(Z_1+\cdots+Z_n)/n$. We prove $\mathbb{P}\{\max_i X_i\le t\}\ge\mathbb{P}\{\sqrt{n/(n-1)}\,\max_i(Z_i-\overline{Z})\le t\}$ for every $t\in\mathbb{R}$, and for each fixed $t>0$ equality holds only when $\mathrm{Cov}(X_i,X_j)=-1/(n-1)$ for all $i\ne j$.
